title: [Bug]: All versions of Electron (chromium upstream bug) fail to open on Ubuntu 24.04+ due to kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1 by default
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [X] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [X] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

All

### What operating system are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 24.04

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

None

### Expected Behavior

Applications built using electron can launch

### Actual Behavior

Applications cannot launch unless they each ship an apparmor override

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

added optionally in Ubuntu 23.10, enabled by default and going forward in Ubuntu 24.04 LTS
https://ubuntu.com/blog/ubuntu-23-10-restricted-unprivileged-user-namespaces

There is a (not public) chromium bug report for this apparently. Maybe electron developers can see and track its progress 
https://<redacted-host>/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=1459821
https://<redacted-host>/ubuntu/+source/linux-meta-nvidia-5.19/+bug/2017980/comments/27
(ignore the package the bug was created under in ubuntu, this has nothing to do with nvidia and affects all kernels)

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
I have the same problem. All apps based on Electron will not be able to run on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS. Tested Motrix and QQ.

If running the app with sudo (also `--no-sandbox`), then will get a blank window with nothing.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
The temporary solution is disabling the kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns:

```
sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0
```

comments.author: participant4
comments.body: This issue is caused by `apparmor`'s default policy, which lacks a specific profile in the `/etc/apparmor.d/` directory. Currently, the workaround is to manually add the profile. you can refer to the latest vscode for guidance.It's not necessary to disable sandbox or modify kernel parameters to resolve this.

comments.author: participant5
participant6
comments.body:
Hi,

I did something like this for mattermost desktop: 

```
 cat /etc/apparmor.d/mattermost-desktop
# This profile allows everything and only exists to give the
# application a name instead of having the label "unconfined"

abi <abi/4.0>,
include <tunables/global>

profile mattermost-desktop /usr/bin/mattermost-desktop flags=(unconfined) {
  userns,

# Site-specific additions and overrides. See local/README for details.
  include if exists <local/mattermost-desktop>
}
```

And it works fine
Hope this help

comments.author: participant12
comments.body:
In the meantime, it would be much better to create a specific AppArmor profile instead of just disabling it system-wide. You can unconfine specific Electron applications like so:

```
abi <abi/4.0>,
include <tunables/global>

profile electron-app /path/to/electron/app flags=(unconfined) {
  userns,
}
```
```
sudo apparmor_parser -r /etc/apparmor.d/electron-app
systemctl --user restart your-electron-app
```
